source.review_note: Exact Yamaha renewal cross-sections visually reviewed at PDF187,189,193,195; Motion Pro tool instruction photographs reviewed on all three pages. Tool examples are different-model technique, never installation-depth authority. Root independently reviewed exact OEM renewal diagrams and all steps with Motion Pro technique; approved after self-contained grease and source-link corrections.

title: Renew swingarm and linkage bearings, then restore the rear assembly
completeness: Four swingarm and six linkage bearings renewed with matched bushes/collars, thrust bearings and new seals; exact depth records and complete bike-level rear assembly closure. Shock eyes/internal damper excluded.

applicability.included: Exact stock2026 US standard YZ450F; all four swingarm pivot bearings, matched bushes, thrust bearings and seals; six linkage bearings with matching collars and seals. Shock eye bearings and sealed shock internals remain unchanged.
excluded: Shock eye bearing or bushing renewal
Replacement chain or non-stock master-link joint

prerequisites: Match the exact bike and installed stock parts. Have the complete cited diagrams available.
Stable maintenance stand and support suitable for changing weight distribution; clean labeled parts storage.
Confirm replacement parts match actual stock assemblies before removal. Verify bearing tool mandrels, receiver and puller fit each joint; no08-0294 model fit is asserted.
Engine separately supported while pivot removed; shock remains supported by unchanged upper mount.

required_tools.name: Secure stand plus independent swingarm/engine/caliper support
Torque tools covering21–135 N·m; axle/pivot/linkage tools
Clip-type chain joint tools and approximately50 N chain measurement tool
Correct-fitting Motion Pro08-0294 suspension bearing tool and illustrated adapters; appropriate wrenches/vise support
Depth measuring tool and straight reference suitable for OEM cross-section dimensions

required_parts.name: New exact stock-chain master-link clip
required_parts.purpose: OEM marks the removed joint clip for replacement; verify chain identity first.

required_parts.name: Four swingarm bearings, two matched bushes, two thrust bearings, four new seals; inspect/replace two collars as needed
required_parts.purpose: Renew complete stock pivot stack; bearing/bushing matched sets perOEM194

required_parts.name: Four relay-arm bearings, two matched collars and four new seals; inspect both four-washer groups
Two connecting-arm bearings, one matched collar and two new seals

critical_stop_conditions: Unstable support, bent/cracked parts, damaged fasteners or unknown assembly order.
Binding, leaks, missing hardware or abnormal brake/control function remains an unresolved fault.

steps.title: Support the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Support the bike with its rear wheel off the ground. Select neutral. Protect the rear brake pedal against operation while the wheel is removed; keep the hydraulic line closed.
verification: Rear wheel clear, bike stable, brake pedal protected.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Release the axle and chain
steps.instruction: Remove the axle nut. Loosen both adjuster locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts inward to let the wheel move forward. Support the wheel, withdraw the axle and retain both pullers and collars by side. Push the wheel forward, lift the chain from the sprocket and remove the wheel without disturbing the hydraulic line.
verification: Wheel clear; left/right pullers and collars labeled.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Inspect wheel, axle and collars
steps.instruction: Check the axle for bending, the tire/wheel and collars for damage, and bearings for roughness or looseness. Inspect seals and sprocket teeth. Record defects; damaged components need the matching repair before refitting.
verification: Serviceability recorded; no damaged parts silently reused.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Open the original clip-type drive chain
steps.instruction: Remove the master-link clip, plate and master link, then remove the chain. Keep its orientation and original matched parts identified. This operation applies to the stock clip-type joint; a riveted or replacement chain requires its maker's joint procedure.
verification: Stock clip joint identified; chain removed; new correct clip ready.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Support the closed rear brake assembly
steps.instruction: Slide the complete rear caliper and bracket free of the swingarm guide after wheel removal. Release the hose retaining clamps shown in the routing diagram and support the assembly without twisting or stretching the hose. Do not remove hose unions, pads or sliding pins. Remove the brake-pedal pivot bolt and unhook its spring to clear pivot access; support the pedal while leaving its master-cylinder linkage attached.
verification: Hose free of swingarm and supported; hydraulics closed; pedal/return spring retained.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Unlink the shock and linkage
steps.instruction: Support the swingarm independently. Remove the lower shock bolt and keep the shock supported on its unchanged upper mount. Remove the connecting-arm frame bolt, connecting-arm-to-relay bolt and relay-to-swingarm bolt, keeping each fastener and collar/washer stack associated with its joint. Identify each linkage assembly for the following renewal steps.
verification: Swingarm cannot drop; three linkage joints and lower shock joint identified.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Withdraw the pivot and swingarm
steps.instruction: Support the engine and frame while leaving all other engine mounts undisturbed. Remove the pivot nut, withdraw the pivot shaft and lower the supported swingarm. Keep the collars and thrust-bearing/seal stack in their original positions. The pivot also passes through the engine rear mount; do not let engine or swingarm weight bind the shaft.
verification: Engine and arm independently supported; pivot and bearing stacks labeled.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Inspect the arm, pivot and linkage
steps.instruction: Inspect swingarm and linkage arms for cracks, bending and damaged bearing bores. Roll the pivot on a flat surface to check straightness; never straighten a bent pivot. Record condition of bushes, collars, thrust bearings and washers. Replace damaged structural parts before installing new bearings. Bearing/bushing and linkage bearing/collar pairs are renewed as sets.
verification: Serviceability recorded for pivot, arm and every linkage joint.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Identify every bearing and seal stack
steps.instruction: Photograph both swingarm ends and each linkage joint against Yamaha PDF187/193. Remove collars, seals, thrust bearings, bushes and washers in illustrated order, retaining identified serviceable washers separately. The swingarm has four pivot bearings; the relay arm has four and connecting arm two. Do not mix washer groups or press against a retained seal, collar or bush.
verification: All stacks mapped to source diagram
Four swingarm and six linkage bearings identified

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Remove bearings with supported fitting tools
steps.instruction: Use Motion Pro08-0294 figures1-2/5 for accessible bearings: select a fitting driver, center the receiver and draw each bearing into the cup. Where opposite-side access is unavailable, figures7-8 show the fully engaged blind remover with greased puller threads/washer. First remove obstructions and check for hidden retainers. Stop if the receiver cannot support the housing squarely. Clean and inspect every empty bore.
verification: Tool fit/support and unobstructed removal path checked
Bores undamaged; no retained debris

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths
Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Install the four pivot bearings to Yamaha depths
steps.instruction: Pack bearings and lubricate the pivot bearing stack with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Motion Pro figures3-4 show a matching mandrel supporting needles during installation. Yamaha PDF194 requires outer bearings first, then inner bearings to the illustrated depths measured from inside. Use PDF193/195 cross-sections: inner bearing position dimension b is6.5mm. Record both sides. Yamaha depths control; do not substitute the CRF example tool-bottoming endpoint.
verification: Four bearings installed outer then inner
Both6.5mm reference dimensions measured at exact OEM section
No needle loss, cocking or damage

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths
Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Complete pivot bushes, thrust bearings and seals
steps.instruction: Restore the two correct new matched bushes, two thrust bearings, four new oil seals and inspected collars in Yamaha PDF193/195 order. Lubricate with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Measure the four illustrated seal recesses a:0–0.5mm from their respective bore faces. Use the cross-section for lip orientation and the general seal markings guidance; do not use the6.5mm bearing depth for a seal. Record each seal depth and stack.
verification: Two bushes/two thrust bearings/four seals accounted for
Four a depths0–0.5mm recorded
Seals undamaged and correctly oriented

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Renew both relay-arm bearing pairs
steps.instruction: Install the four relay bearings using fitting mandrels and supported housing. Yamaha PDF187/189 specifies0mm bearing depth at the illustrated end faces. Lubricate bearings, washers, seals and collars with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Restore inner washers, four new seals, matched collars and outer washers in the exact exploded/cross-section order. Record bearing flushness and both four-washer groups; the bearing0mm dimension is not a generic seal-depth instruction.
verification: Four relay bearings at source0mm faces
Four inner and four outer washers correctly grouped
Four new seals and two matched collars installed

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Renew connecting-arm bearings
steps.instruction: Install the two connecting-arm bearings at the0mm bearing locations illustrated on Yamaha PDF187/189. Use molybdenum-disulfide grease at the exploded-diagram marked bearing/seal/collar surfaces. Restore two new seals and the matched collar with source orientation. Record both bearing positions and smooth collar movement; do not infer a seal depth from the bearing dimension.
verification: Two connecting bearings flush at specified faces
Two new seals and matched collar installed
No binding or displaced seal

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Grease and position the swingarm
steps.instruction: Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the pivot, bearing contact surfaces, thrust bearings, bushings, collars and seals per the diagram. Confirm the renewed bearing stacks and collars are correctly installed, then return the arm. Insert the pivot from the right. Apply lithium-soap grease to the pivot-nut threads and contact face and tighten the pivot nut to 75 N·m.
verification: Correct grease locations; original stack order; pivot from right; nut 75 N·m.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Refit the linkage in its original orientation
steps.instruction: Lubricate the circumferences and threads of the three linkage bolts and lower shock bolt with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Fit the connecting-arm frame bolt from the right; connecting-arm relay bolt, relay-arm swingarm bolt and lower shock bolt from the left. Restore each correct new matched collar and inspected washer in its identified joint. Raise the arm to align the lower shock without forcing the bolts.
verification: Original linkage orientation and washer stacks restored; bolt directions matched.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Secure the linkage and lower shock
steps.instruction: Tighten the connecting-arm frame nut and connecting-arm relay nut to 80 N·m each. Tighten the relay-arm swingarm nut to 70 N·m and the lower shock nut to 53 N·m. The unchanged upper shock mount is not part of this removal.
verification: Frame 80, relay 80, swingarm 70, lower shock 53 N·m recorded.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Restore pedal and hose routing
steps.instruction: Refit the pedal with its original spring and grease the pivot contact/seal locations shown with lithium-soap grease. Tighten the pedal pivot bolt to 26 N·m. Route the brake hose clear of the spring and suspension without twist; its paint mark faces upward. Fully seat the hose clamps in their bases, engage each lock by at least three notches and face their openings inward. Keep the complete caliper bracket supported for wheel installation.
verification: Pedal 26 N·m; spring restored; hose/retainers matched; no open hydraulics.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Reconnect the stock chain
steps.instruction: Fit the original matched master link and plate with a new correct master-link clip. Follow the OEM diagram so the closed end of the clip leads in the chain's direction of travel. Lubricate the chain. Do not reuse the removed clip or apply this procedure to a different chain joint.
verification: New matching clip fully seated with closed end leading chain travel.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and chain
steps.instruction: Grease the oil-seal lips with lithium-soap-based grease and refit the collars. Place the disc between the brake pads and locate the caliper bracket correctly in its swingarm guide. Push the wheel forward and put the chain onto the sprocket. Fit the left puller and insert the greased axle from the left.
verification: Collars retained; bracket engaged; disc between pads; chain on sprocket; axle from left.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Fit the right puller and nut
steps.instruction: Fit the right chain puller, washer and axle nut. Leave the nut temporarily snug until chain adjustment is complete.
verification: Right puller and washer present; axle nut temporary only.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Measure and adjust chain slack
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel raised and gearbox in neutral, pull the chain upward above the chain-guide mounting bolt with about 50 N. Measure between the drive-chain guide and the bottom of the chain at the exact diagram location. Adjust both sides equally to 50–60 mm. Push the wheel forward so each puller/end plate is seated against the swingarm end.
verification: Measured slack 50–60 mm using OEM50 N reference; pullers equally adjusted and seated.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Secure the rear axle and adjusters
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m and both chain-adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m. Recheck the chain slack after tightening.
verification: Axle 135 N·m; locknuts 21 N·m; final slack recorded.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Check chain alignment and brake function
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel and check the chain follows the sprockets, the brake disc sits correctly and the rear brake has normal firm operation. Record wheel installation and any unresolved fault before use.
verification: Alignment, wheel rotation and brake action verified.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Verify the complete rear assembly
steps.instruction: Check rear suspension travel for smooth movement, no side play or binding, brake hose clearance, chain alignment/slack and normal firm rear-brake action. Record all disturbed fasteners and any defect. Wheel refit alone does not verify the linkage; record this separate check.
verification: Suspension, chain and brake checks recorded; no unresolved defect hidden.
steps.origin: Original OEM-based summary; record prompts and sealed-assembly handling are explicit workshop workflow adaptations.

entry_state: Assembled stock bike with verified replacement parts and fitting bearing tools; engine supported independently before pivot removal.
exit_state: Swingarm pivot and connecting/relay arm bearing stacks renewed and depths recorded; wheel, chain, closed brake and linkage refitted; rear suspension movement and all closure checks recorded.
